facts.fact_text: On 30 March 2004 the second applicant and two other members of Ilinden notified the Mayor of Sandanski that the organisation intended to stage a rally on 18 April 2004.
The rally notified on 30 March 2004 was planned to take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on 18 April 2004 at the grave of Yane Sandanski near the Rozhen Monastery.
The purpose of the rally notified on 30 March 2004 was to commemorate the anniversary of Yane Sandanski's "dastardly murder".
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include laying flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski.
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include making speeches about the life and activity of Yane Sandanski.
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2004 would include a "cultural programme".
On 19 April 2004 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally at 3 p.m. on 4 May 2004 in front of the monument to Gotse Delchev in Blagoevgrad.
The purpose of the rally notified on 19 April 2004 was to commemorate the anniversary of Gotse Delchev's assassination by laying flowers.
The rally notified on 19 April 2004 was described as being in front of the monument to "the great Macedonian revolutionary" Gotse Delchev in Blagoevgrad.
The rally notified on 19 April 2004 would start in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad and make its way to Macedonia Square, where the monument to Gotse Delchev was located.

On 30 March 2006 the second applicant and two other members of Ilinden notified the Mayor of Sandanski that the organisation intended to stage a rally between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. on 23 April 2006 at the grave of Yane Sandanski near the Rozhen Monastery, to commemorate the anniversary of his "dastardly murder".
The planned rally notified on 30 March 2006 would include laying flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski, a speech about his life and activity, and a "cultural programme".

In a letter of 18 April 2006 the Mayor of Sandanski informed Ilinden that it could lay flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski and organise a cultural programme between 10 a.m. and 12 noon on 23 April 2006.
On 23 April 2006 members and supporters of Ilinden gathered in front of Yane Sandanski's grave near the Rozhen Monastery.

According to the applicants, at about 10.30 a.m. on 18 April 2004 a plain-clothes police officer, accompanied by two uniformed police officers, approached the organisers and told them to stop decorating the stage.

According to the applicants, the plain-clothes police officer told the organisers on 18 April 2004 that the Mayor's permission was valid only until 12 noon and that after that they were to leave the area.
After the tension on 18 April 2004, the rally was allowed to proceed.
On 12 September 2004 two plain-clothes police officers approached the leaders of the Ilinden rally and asked them to leave the placards and banners they were carrying.
At about 3 p.m. on 12 September 2004 the participants in the Ilinden rally marched to Macedonia Square, holding up one flag and three placards.
On 12 September 2004 the participants in the Ilinden rally were surrounded by police, who apparently told them several times to put the flag and the placards down.
On 12 September 2004 about eighty metres from the monument to Gotse Delchev, a group of some forty police officers stopped the participants in the Ilinden rally.

On 12 September 2005 approximately thirty uniformed and plain-clothes police officers surrounded the Ilinden members and supporters gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad, blocked their way, seized the flags and placards they were carrying, and destroyed a wreath.
According to the Government, the actions of the police on 12 September 2005 were monitored by a public prosecutor, who did not note any abuse of their powers.
After the police intervention on 12 September 2005, the participants in the Ilinden rally decided not to go to Macedonia Square.

In a letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad informed Ilinden that every citizen of the Republic of Bulgaria had the right to pay his respects to the memory of national heroes and lay flowers at their monuments.
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that in the way it had been planned, the rally was in fact a procession.
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the rally was likely to cause breaches of public order and unrest, as had happened in the past.
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the holding of rallies presupposed registration, proof of which Ilinden had not presented.

In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had planned a children's holiday on Macedonia Square for 4 May 2006, which made the holding of Ilinden's rally impossible.
On 4 May 2006 the police prevented the participants in the Ilinden rally from moving towards Macedonia Square.

On 4 May 2006 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the Ilinden participants in writing to refrain from participating in assemblies without permission from the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.

On 4 May 2006 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the Ilinden participants in writing not to use placards, banners and other visual materials featuring texts with anti-Bulgarian content.
The Ilinden rally proceeded on 30 July 2006 at Samuilova Krepost and was attended by about two hundred and fifteen people.
According to the Government, the only incident at the rally on 30 July 2006 was an attempt by a member of Ilinden to damage the film camera of a local television station.

According to the applicants, the same member of Ilinden was kicked three times in the legs by a police officer on 30 July 2006 while trying to prevent the officer from entering a restaurant where the participants in the rally were dining.
On 30 August 2006 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to hold a rally on Macedonia Square at 4 p.m. on 12 September 2006.
On 30 August 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the event planned for 12 September 2006 could not proceed, as it might breach public order and infringe the rights of others.

On 4 September 2006 a member of Ilinden's managing council notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad again of the organisation's intention to hold a rally on 12 September 2006, to commemorate "the victims of the Macedonian nation following the Bulgarian governments' acts of State terrorism and genocide".

In the notification of 4 September 2006, the member of Ilinden's managing council stated that for years on end the Mayor of Blagoevgrad had prevented Ilinden from staging rallies, relying on bogus arguments.
In a letter of 5 September 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the notification could not be examined, as no documents proving that Ilinden had been registered had been produced.
In the letter of 5 September 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that it was impossible to identify the "members of the managing bodies of [the] event" due to the lack of registration documents.

In the letter of 5 September 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had organised a school holiday at Macedonia Square on 12 September 2006, which made the holding of Ilinden's rally impossible.
On 7 September 2006 Ilinden sought judicial review of the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2006 by the Blagoevgrad District Court.
In a final decision of 8 September 2006 the Blagoevgrad District Court rejected Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2006.
The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 8 September 2006 that the risk of breaches of public order had not been made out by the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 8 September 2006 that, in the light of the European Court of Human Rights' judgments in a series of cases against Bulgaria, the lack of registration was not a sufficient ground to ban a rally.
The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 8 September 2006 that the holding of a school holiday prevented the parallel holding of Ilinden's rally on 12 September 2006.

The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in its decision of 8 September 2006 that it was inopportune to allow adults and children to gather at the same time and place, to concurrently stage a school event and a political one, as "the children's fragile minds should not be subjected to the political interventions and influences which would inevitably occur if the two events [were] allowed to proceed together".
On 8 September 2006 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad that it was willing to reschedule its rally for 4 p.m. on 11 September 2006.
On 8 September 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied to Ilinden's rescheduling notification that it could not be examined, as no documents proving that Ilinden had been registered had been produced.

According to the applicants, as a result of the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's refusals, Ilinden decided not to hold an event on 12 September 2006; only one member laid flowers at the monument to Gotse Delchev.
According to the Government, the rally on 12 September 2006 did take place without hindrance from the police.
Ilinden complained about the Mayor of Sandanski's refusal to let it use the hall to the Commission for Protection against Discrimination, but to no avail.
Ilinden complained about the Mayor of Sandanski's refusal to let it use the hall to the Blagoevgrad Regional Governor, but to no avail.
As a result of the refusal to let it use the municipal hall, Ilinden apparently did not hold the founding meeting as planned.
According to the applicants, on 15 October 2006 the municipal hall in Sandanski was not hosting a sports event, but was empty.

According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 three members of Ilinden were collecting declarations by persons who wished to become members of the political party at a stall in the centre of Sandanski.

According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 two men approached the three Ilinden members at the stall in Sandanski, one of whom was the head of the Petrich chapter of the political party Attack, who shouted insults at them.

According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 the head of the Petrich chapter of the political party Attack threw the materials on the stall to the ground, hit one of the members of Ilinden in the face, and tore apart an Ilinden poster.
According to the applicants, on 19 December 2006 the head of the Petrich chapter of the political party Attack called the police after the assault.
According to the applicants, the police arrived on 19 December 2006 and arrested the attacker.
According to the applicants, the attacker was warned not to engage in violent actions and released on 19 December 2006.
On 19 December 2006 the three members of Ilinden complained about the assault to the prosecuting authorities.

In a decision of 25 January 2007 the Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office refused to open a criminal investigation into the assault of 19 December 2006, as the acts alleged in the complaint did not constitute publicly prosecutable offences.

The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the bodily injuries suffered by the first Ilinden member were minor and therefore gave cause for a private prosecution only.

The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the destroyed property was not of great value, making its destruction a trivial occurrence which should not be criminally prosecuted.
The Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office stated in its decision of 25 January 2007 that the proffering of insults also gave cause for a private prosecution only.

On appeal by the three Ilinden members, on 5 February 2007 the Blagoevgrad Regional Prosecutor's Office upheld the Sandanski District Prosecutor's Office decision of 25 January 2007, fully endorsing its reasoning.

On 16 March 2007 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Sandanski that it intended to stage a rally between 10.30 a.m. and 2 p.m. on 22 April 2007 at the grave of Yane Sandanski near the Rozhen Monastery, to commemorate the anniversary of his "dastardly murder".
The planned rally notified on 16 March 2007 would include laying flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski, a speech about his life and activity, and a "cultural programme".

On 16 March 2007 the Mayor of Sandanski informed Ilinden that he could not agree to the rally planned for 22 April 2007, as he had already allowed a sister organisation, UMO Ilinden – PIRIN, to stage an event at the grave of Yane Sandanski between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on 22 April 2007.

On 26 March 2007 Ilinden informed the Mayor of Sandanski that UMO Ilinden – PIRIN would in fact be holding their event in the town of Melnik, in front of Yane Sandanski's monument, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., and that only a small delegation would go to the grave near the Rozhen Monastery to lay flowers between 10 and 11 a.m.
On 26 March 2007 Ilinden proposed to the Mayor of Sandanski to stage their rally at the grave of Yane Sandanski after 11 a.m.
On 26 March 2007 the Mayor of Sandanski informed Ilinden that the rally could take place between 11 a.m. and 12 noon, as the police did not have the means of protecting a longer event.
As a result of the Mayor of Sandanski's restriction, Ilinden decided to change the date of its rally to 21 April 2007 and notified the Mayor accordingly.

On 27 March 2007 the Mayor of Sandanski replied that he could not accommodate Ilinden's wish to hold the rally on 21 April 2007, as a vocational training school had already applied for, and been given, permission to stage an event at that time.
On 28 March 2007 Ilinden filed an application for judicial review with the Sandanski District Court, arguing that the Mayor of Sandanski's refusals to allow the rally as planned were unlawful.
In its application of 28 March 2007, Ilinden argued that it was willing to shift the timing of the event but could not shrink it into the short timeframe allowed by the Mayor of Sandanski.
In its application of 28 March 2007, Ilinden asked the Sandanski District Court to set aside the Mayor's decisions and allow the rally to be staged between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. on 22 April 2007.
In a decision of 2 April 2007 the Sandanski District Court declared Ilinden's application for judicial review inadmissible.

The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 2 April 2007 that the Mayor of Sandanski had not banned the rally but merely proposed a change in its timing, as was his duty under section 12(1) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act.
The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 2 April 2007 that only bans on rallies were reviewable by the courts, and only after such bans had been appealed against to the municipal council.
The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 2 April 2007 that the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act did not give the courts jurisdiction to allow the holding of rallies.

On 6 April 2007 Ilinden appealed to the Blagoevgrad Regional Court against the Sandanski District Court's decision of 2 April 2007, relying inter alia on the European Court of Human Rights' judgment in Ivanov and Others v. Bulgaria (no. 46336/99, 24 November 2005).
On 18 April 2007 the Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad, acting of his own motion, annulled the Mayor of Sandanski's letter of 26 March 2007 allowing the Ilinden rally.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad reasoned in his decision of 18 April 2007 that the Mayor of Sandanski's letter of 26 March 2007 amounted to an administrative decision creating legal rights for Ilinden and that it was unlawful.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that Ilinden was not registered and that in February 2007 the Supreme Court of Cassation had upheld the Sofia City Court's judgment turning down a request by UMO Ilinden – PIRIN to be registered as a political party (as described in UMO Ilinden – PIRIN and Others v. Bulgaria (no. 2), no. 41561/07, §§ 8-19, 18 October 2011).
The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that since Ilinden was unlawful under Bulgarian law, it had no standing to give notice of its intention to hold a rally.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that the proposed rally would put public order at risk, as the Rozhen Monastery was visited by many tourists, especially at weekends.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that rallies and meetings were being organised at the Rozhen Monastery location at the same time by local authorities and non-governmental organisations.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that as clashes between supporters of Ilinden and others had taken place in the past, it was necessary to ban Ilinden's rally.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that the activities of Ilinden were contrary to Bulgarian law, as they consisted in propaganda against the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity and aroused national and ethnic hatred.
According to the applicants, on 22 April 2007 many bus companies hired to transport participants in the Ilinden rally to the Rozhen Monastery desisted, under pressure from the police.
According to the applicants, on 22 April 2007 two cars carrying materials for a stage to be erected at the site of the rally were stopped by the police and not allowed to continue.
According to the applicants, on 22 April 2007 a bus transporting a group of singers was diverted by the police.
According to the applicants, on 22 April 2007 a number of other cars with participants were stopped and searched by the police while en route to Rozhen Monastery.

According to the applicants, on 22 April 2007 the grave of Yane Sandanski was surrounded by about a hundred uniformed police officers and a number of plain-clothes ones, who did not allow the participants in the rally to approach it.
According to the applicants, no other organisations were present at the grave of Yane Sandanski on 22 April 2007.

According to the Government, Ilinden was able to hold the rally on 22 April 2007, in the presence of many Macedonian journalists and representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the "former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia".

According to the Government, the alleged difficulties with the transportation of the participants on 22 April 2007 were overblown and the police had done nothing more than to ensure the smooth commemoration by various organisations of the anniversary of Yane Sandanski's death.
According to the Government, it was not true that participants in the rally on 22 April 2007 had been stopped and searched.
On 26 April 2007 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, at 4 p.m. on 4 May 2007.

The rally notified on 26 April 2007 was to mark the anniversary of the assassination of Gotse Delchev, described as a "Macedonian revolutionary", and would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers on the monument and a short speech, lasting one hour.
On 26 April 2007 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the notification could not be examined as Ilinden had not produced documents proving its official registration.
On 26 April 2007 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that it was impossible to identify the "managing bodies of [the] event" due to the lack of registration documents.
On 26 April 2007 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that on 4 May 2007 the municipality was organising children's games on Macedonia Square, so that the staging of Ilinden's event could not be allowed.

Ilinden filed an application for judicial review of the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's decision with the Blagoevgrad District Court, arguing that there was no risk that breaches of public order or traffic disturbances would occur.
In its application for judicial review, Ilinden argued that Macedonia Square was very large and Ilinden was planning to use only a small part of it for its rally.

In its application for judicial review, Ilinden argued that the ban was not justified under section 12(2) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act or Article 11 § 2 of the Convention and was in breach of Ilinden's right to express its opinion under Article 10 of the Convention.
In a final decision of 27 April 2007 the Blagoevgrad District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the rally planned for 4 May 2007.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 27 April 2007 that while the lack of registration did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally, the risk that it could infringe the rights of others was enough to justify the ban.

The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in its decision of 27 April 2007 that it was inopportune to allow adults and children to gather at the same time and place, to concurrently stage a school event and a political one, as "the children should not be subjected to the political interventions and influences which would inevitably occur if the two events [were] allowed to proceed together".

On 3 May 2007 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered in writing a member of Ilinden's leadership not to organise or take part in a rally on 4 May 2007.
According to the Government, on 4 May 2007 members of Ilinden laid flowers at the monument to Gotse Delchev without being stopped by the police.

On 16 July 2007 the head of Ilinden's chapter in Petrich notified the Mayor of Petrich that the organisation intended to stage a rally in the area of Samuilova Krepost at 10 a.m. on 29 July 2007, to mark the anniversary of the Ilinden uprising.

In a letter of 22 July 2004 the Mayor of Petrich advised Ilinden that VMRO had already applied for and been granted permission to hold an event at Samuilova Krepost at the same place and at the same time as Ilinden's planned rally on 29 July 2007.
On 20 July 2007 Ilinden sought judicial review of the Mayor of Petrich's decision by the Petrich District Court, arguing that both events could proceed simultaneously.
In a decision of 25 July 2007 the Petrich District Court declared Ilinden's application for judicial review inadmissible.

The Petrich District Court held in its decision of 25 July 2007 that the Mayor of Petrich's letter did not amount to a ban, but merely to information that another rally had been planned for the same time and place.

The Petrich District Court held in its decision of 25 July 2007 that under the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act, if a rally had not been banned within twenty-four hours of notice being given to the Mayor, it could proceed.

The Petrich District Court held in its decision of 25 July 2007 that even if the Mayor did ban a rally, that decision first had to be appealed against to the municipal council and only then challenged by way of judicial review.
On 29 July 2007 about three hundred and fifty members and supporters of Ilinden approached Samuilova Krepost, carrying placards and banners.
According to the applicants, on 29 July 2007 the Ilinden participants were stopped by the police before reaching Samuilova Krepost and were ordered to put the placards and banners down.
According to the applicants, the Ilinden participants obeyed the police order on 29 July 2007 and were allowed access to Samuilova Krepost without the materials.
On 29 July 2007 the participants in the Ilinden rally laid wreaths and flowers at Samuilova Krepost.
On 29 July 2007 a plain-clothes police officer removed the ribbons from the wreaths laid by the Ilinden participants at Samuilova Krepost.

On 29 July 2007 the Ilinden participants tried to erect a stage at their chosen place at Samuilova Krepost but were stopped by the police and so erected it on the other side of a small river crossing the site.
According to the Government, the police did not impose restrictions on the manner of commemorating the anniversary at Samuilova Krepost on 29 July 2007.
On 28 August 2007 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, at 4.30 p.m. on 12 September 2007.

The rally notified on 28 August 2007 was to mark the anniversary of "the genocide against the Macedonians" and would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers on the monument and a short speech, lasting one hour.
On 29 August 2007 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the notification could not be examined as Ilinden had not produced documents proving its official registration.

On 29 August 2007 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had planned a children's holiday under the name "Hello, school" on Macedonia Square for 12 September 2007, to mark the beginning of the school year, which made the holding of Ilinden's rally impossible.
On 30 August 2007 Ilinden sought judicial review of the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's decision by the newly created Blagoevgrad Administrative Court.

In a decision of 30 August 2007 the Blagoevgrad Administrative Court found that under the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act, which was lex specialis in relation to the general rules of administrative procedure, the court competent to examine an application for judicial review of a Mayor's decision to ban a rally was the district court.
The Blagoevgrad Administrative Court sent the file to the Blagoevgrad District Court in its decision of 30 August 2007.
In a final decision of 5 September 2007 the Blagoevgrad District Court dismissed Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007.

The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 5 September 2007 that while the lack of registration did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally, the fact that another event likely to draw a number of people, many of whom were children, was due to take place on the same date in Macedonia Square was enough to justify the ban.
According to the applicants, no school event took place at 4 p.m. on 12 September 2007 on Macedonia Square in Blagoevgrad.

According to the applicants, when a number of members and supporters of Ilinden gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad at about 5 p.m. on 12 September 2007, they were stopped by the police and a number of them were arrested.

According to the applicants, the arrested Ilinden members on 12 September 2007 were taken to a police station, held for about three hours, and charged with committing administrative offences for having tried to take part in a banned rally.

On 22 October 2007 the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad imposed administrative fines of 200 Bulgarian levs (102.26 euros) each on the second applicant and on a number of members of Ilinden for having taken part in a banned rally, in breach of a public-order regulation issued by the Blagoevgrad Municipal Council.
The second applicant and the members of Ilinden fined on 22 October 2007 all sought judicial review of the fines.
In a series of judgments delivered on 18 and 19 February, 11 March, and 22 and 29 May 2008 the Blagoevgrad District Court annulled the fines imposed on 22 October 2007.

In some of the judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the fines were invalid as under the applicable rules the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad had no power to impose administrative punishments.

In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the deputy Mayor's decisions were defective because they did not specify which administrative offences had been committed.

In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that although the Mayor's ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007 was legally binding, the actions of the members of Ilinden on that date had not amounted to the staging of a rally, as they had been too few and had not tried to wave banners and make speeches, but merely to lay flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument.
The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in those judgments that every person, regardless of their political convictions, had the right to honour the memory of national heroes in peace.

On 4 March 2008 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Sandanski that it intended to stage a rally between 10.30 a.m. and 3 p.m. on 20 April 2008 at the grave of Yane Sandanski near the Rozhen Monastery, to commemorate the anniversary of his murder.
The planned rally notified on 4 March 2008 would include laying flowers at the grave of Yane Sandanski, a speech about his life and work, and a "literary and musical programme".

On 17 March 2008 the Mayor of Sandanski advised Ilinden that its members could lay flowers on the grave of Yane Sandanski between 10.30 and 11 a.m. on 20 April 2008, but not carry out the remainder of their programme, as an event had been planned for that date by a vocational training school.

On 26 March 2008 Ilinden sought judicial review by the Sandanski District Court, arguing that there was enough room for both its and the school's events and that the limitations imposed by the Mayor of Sandanski hindered the exercise of its right of peaceful assembly.
In a decision of 17 April 2008 the Sandanski District Court found that Ilinden's application for judicial review was inadmissible.

The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 17 April 2008 that the Mayor of Sandanski had not banned the rally but merely proposed a change in its timing, as was his duty under section 12(1) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act.

The Sandanski District Court held in its decision of 17 April 2008 that only bans on rallies were reviewable by the courts, and only after such bans had been appealed against to the municipal council, and that the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act did not give the courts jurisdiction to allow the holding of rallies.

On 17 April 2008 the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the second applicant to abide by the limitations imposed by the Mayor of Sandanski, to ensure public order during the event, not to urge a violent change of the constitutional order, and not to incite the commission of offences through public speeches.
According to the applicants, on 20 April 2008 the police stopped a number of cars travelling to Rozhen to take part in the Ilinden rally.
According to the applicants, the grave of Yane Sandanski was surrounded by about thirty police officers on 20 April 2008.

According to the applicants, on 20 April 2008 one police officer wanted to remove the ribbons from a wreath which members of Ilinden wished to lay on the grave of Yane Sandanski, which sparked off a forceful verbal exchange.

On 1 September 2008 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 12 September 2008, to commemorate "the genocide against the Macedonians perpetrated by Bulgarian State terrorism".
The rally notified on 1 September 2008 would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, the making of a short speech, and the lighting of candles.
The Mayor of Blagoevgrad did not reply to Ilinden's notification of 1 September 2008.
A number of members and supporters of Ilinden gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad at about 4.40 p.m. on 12 September 2008.
The Ilinden members and supporters gathered on 12 September 2008 carried two posters saying "UMO Ilinden" and "12 September – Day of the Genocide of the Macedonians of Bulgaria".
Several uniformed and plain-clothes police officers appeared at the scene in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad ten minutes after the Ilinden members gathered on 12 September 2008.
On 12 September 2008 one police officer told the Ilinden participants that if they carried posters "which are against Bulgaria" the posters would be taken away.
On 12 September 2008 the police seized the poster bearing the inscription "12 September – Day of the Genocide of the Macedonians of Bulgaria" from the Ilinden participants.
On 12 September 2008 the participants in the Ilinden rally headed towards Macedonia Square in Blagoevgrad.

On the way to Macedonia Square on 12 September 2008, two men threatened one of the Ilinden participants, saying "we will now fine you 200 [Bulgarian] levs each, I know your sons, we will fire them from work ...".
On 12 September 2008 the members of Ilinden stood in front of Gotse Delchev's monument on Macedonia Square, laid a wreath and flowers, and lit candles.
On 12 September 2008 one member of Ilinden made a short speech at Gotse Delchev's monument on Macedonia Square.
The police did not interfere with the Ilinden event at Macedonia Square on 12 September 2008.
After the Ilinden event on 12 September 2008, the police arrested a member of Ilinden who was taking photographs, took his camera by force, and exposed the film in it.

On 24 April 2009 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, at 5 p.m. on 4 May 2009, to mark the anniversary of Gotse Delchev's death.

In a letter delivered to Ilinden's chairman at 4.30 p.m. on 30 April 2009 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad informed the organisation that they could join the laying of flowers in front of Gotse Delchev's monument at 10 a.m. on 4 May 2009, together with representatives of other political and civic organisations.
In view of the short time until the date of the planned event, Ilinden did not seek judicial review of the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's decision communicated on 30 April 2009.
The second applicant and two other members of Ilinden tried to approach Gotse Delchev's monument at 2.40 p.m. on 4 May 2009.
The second applicant and two other members of Ilinden were arrested and taken to a police station on 4 May 2009.

At the police station on 4 May 2009, the second applicant and two other members of Ilinden were issued orders under section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act not to take part in the rally prohibited by the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.
On 4 May 2009 the police seized a wreath with a ribbon saying "To Gotse from UMO Ilinden" from the Ilinden members.

On 31 August 2009 Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally in Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, between 12 noon and 1 p.m. on 12 September 2009, to mark the "day of the genocide against the Macedonian people".
The Mayor of Blagoevgrad did not reply to Ilinden's notification of 31 August 2009.
On 12 September 2009 members and supporters of Ilinden gathered in front of Gotse Delchev's monument on Macedonia Square in Blagoevgrad but were arrested and taken to a police station.

At the police station on 12 September 2009, the police, relying on section 55 of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, ordered the second applicant and six other members of Ilinden's leadership not to take part in rallies not authorised by the Mayor of Blagoevgrad.
On 12 September 2009 the police seized from the Ilinden members a ribbon bearing the inscription "12.IX. Day of the genocide against the Macedonian people".
On 12 September 2009 the police seized from the Ilinden members a poster bearing the inscription "12.IX. Day of the genocide against the Macedonian people".
On 12 September 2009 the police seized from the Ilinden members a red flag bearing the inscription "Macedonia" and depicting the "Star of Vergina".

Section 12(3) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the prohibition shall be imposed by a written reasoned act not later than twenty-four hours following the notification.

Section 12(4) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that the organiser of the meeting, demonstration or march may appeal to the Executive Committee of the People's Council against the prohibition, and the Executive Committee shall decide within twenty-four hours.

Section 12(5) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that where the Executive Committee of the People's Council has not decided within the time-limit, the march, demonstration or meeting may proceed.

Section 12(6) of the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act provided that if the appeal is dismissed the dispute shall be referred to the relevant district court which shall decide within five days, and that court's decision shall be final.

The 1990 Meetings and Marches Act was adopted when the 1971 Constitution was in force, under which the executive local State authorities were the executive committees of the people's councils in each district.

The 1991 Constitution abolished the executive committees of the people's councils and established the post of mayor, elected by direct universal suffrage, as the "organ of the executive power in the municipality" under Article 139.
Under section 62(1) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, the police could, if necessary for the performance of their duties, issue orders to individuals or organisations.
Under section 62(4) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, orders issued by the police were binding unless they obviously imposed the commission of an offence.
Section 62(5) of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act provided that police orders, when issued in writing, were subject to judicial review.

Section 55(1), (4) and (5) of the 2006 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act, which superseded section 62 of the 1997 Ministry of Internal Affairs Act on 1 May 2006, has almost identical wording and is currently in force.
In the letter of 20 April 2004, the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the rally was likely to stir unrest and breaches of public order, as had happened in the past.
In the letter of 20 April 2004, the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the holding of rallies presupposed registration, proof of which Ilinden had not presented.
In the letter of 20 April 2004, the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that to proclaim Gotse Delchev a "Macedonian revolutionary" was "unconstitutional and provocative".
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the rally was likely to cause breaches of public order and unrest, as had happened in the past.
In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the holding of rallies presupposed registration, proof of which Ilinden had not presented.

In the letter of 25 April 2006 the Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had planned a children's holiday on Macedonia Square for 4 May 2006, which made the holding of Ilinden's rally impossible.
The Blagoevgrad District Court held in its decision of 8 September 2006 that the holding of a school holiday prevented the parallel holding of Ilinden's rally on 12 September 2006.

The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in its decision of 8 September 2006 that it was inopportune to allow adults and children to gather at the same time and place, to concurrently stage a school event and a political one, as "the children's fragile minds should not be subjected to the political interventions and influences which would inevitably occur if the two events [were] allowed to proceed together".

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that the proposed rally would put public order at risk, as the Rozhen Monastery was visited by many tourists, especially at weekends.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that rallies and meetings were being organised at the Rozhen Monastery location at the same time by local authorities and non-governmental organisations.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that as clashes between supporters of Ilinden and others had taken place in the past, it was necessary to ban Ilinden's rally.

The Regional Governor of Blagoevgrad stated in his decision of 18 April 2007 that the activities of Ilinden were contrary to Bulgarian law, as they consisted in propaganda against the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity and aroused national and ethnic hatred.

In a decision of 1 December 2005 the Sofia Regional Military Prosecutor's Office refused to open a criminal investigation into the police actions on 12 September 2005, reasoning that there was no indication that the police officers had acted unlawfully in preventing the rally or in impounding the objects carried by the participants.
Ilinden's appeal against the Sofia Regional Military Prosecutor's Office decision of 1 December 2005 was rejected by the Military Appellate Prosecutor's Office on 16 January 2006.
In a series of judgments delivered on 18 and 19 February, 11 March, and 22 and 29 May 2008 the Blagoevgrad District Court annulled the fines imposed on 22 October 2007.

In some of the judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the fines were invalid as under the applicable rules the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad had no power to impose administrative punishments.

In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the deputy Mayor's decisions were defective because they did not specify which administrative offences had been committed.

In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that although the Mayor's ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007 was legally binding, the actions of the members of Ilinden on that date had not amounted to the staging of a rally, as they had been too few and had not tried to wave banners and make speeches, but merely to lay flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument.
The Blagoevgrad District Court stated in those judgments that every person, regardless of their political convictions, had the right to honour the memory of national heroes in peace.
